Run the simulation

Source: R/model.R
run_simulation.Rd

Run the simulation

Usage

run_simulation(parameters_list, state = NULL)

Arguments

parameters_list

A list of model parameters as generated by get_parameters()

state

Optional simulation state from a previous run, as returned in the state element of the output list. When provided, the simulation resumes from this state. simulation_time controls the number of additional timesteps to run (not the absolute end time). With time-varying transmission, beta vectors are indexed by day from the start of the original run, so they must have a value for every day up to the end of the resumed run. The population is rebuilt from the seed saved in the state, so parameters_list$seed must be NULL or that same seed, and the population parameters must not change. The random number streams continue from the state, so a run resumed from a state matches an uninterrupted run. Default is NULL (start fresh).

Value

A list with two elements:

result

A data frame of simulation outputs with one row per timestep simulated in this call. When resuming, timestep counts from the start of the original run, so the results of successive calls can be joined with rbind(). The columns are described below.

state

The final simulation state, which can be passed to a subsequent call to resume the simulation. A list with elements timesteps (the number of timesteps simulated so far), individual (the state of the individual package's variables, events and base R's random number generator), dqrng (dqrng's random number state) and seed (the seed that built the population, drawn at random when parameters_list$seed is NULL).

The result data frame always contains the following columns:

  • timestep: The simulation timestep index.

  • S_count: The number of individuals in the Susceptible disease state.

  • E_count: The number of individuals in the Exposed (infected but not yet infectious) disease state.

  • I_count: The number of individuals in the Infectious disease state.

  • I_mild_count: The number of individuals in the mild Infectious disease state.

  • I_hosp_count: The number of individuals in the severe Infectious disease state that require hospitalization.

  • R_count: The number of individuals in the Recovered (immune) disease state.

  • D_count: The number of individuals in the Death state.

  • E_new: The number of individuals newly transitioning from Susceptible to Exposed (i.e. new infections) at each timestep.

When endemic_or_epidemic = "endemic", an additional column is included:

  • n_external_infections: The number of susceptible individuals infected via the external/background infection source at each timestep.

When render_diagnostics = TRUE, additional diagnostic columns are included:

  • FOI_household: The maximum force of infection from household contacts across all individuals at each timestep.

  • FOI_workplace: The maximum force of infection from workplace contacts across all individuals at each timestep.

  • FOI_school: The maximum force of infection from school contacts across all individuals at each timestep.

  • FOI_leisure: The maximum force of infection from leisure setting contacts across all individuals at each timestep.

  • FOI_community: The community-level force of infection (derived from global prevalence) at each timestep.

  • FOI_total: The maximum total force of infection (sum across all settings) experienced by any individual at each timestep.

See also
